newsitem.title: USA: Viacom net losses rise after restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Viacom net losses rise after restructuring charge.

text.p: Viacom Inc. said Tuesday its losses soared in the fourth quarter after the giant entertainment and publishing company decided to leave the interactive game business and took a restructuring charge for its Blockbuster video store unit.

Viacom said, however, that its operating income grew, led by MTV Networks and Paramount Pictures, which enjoyed strong performances from the movies "Mission: Impossible," "Star Trek: First Contact," and "The First Wives Club."

Viacom's losses rose to $242.4 million, or 68 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $10.5 million, or 3 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues rose to $3.4 billion from $2.8 billion.
In January, Viacom said it would report a charge to close about 50 underperforming Blockbuster Music stores, or about 10 percent of the chain's outlets.

Excluding the $98 million charge, Viacom's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and other items surged 32 percent for the quarter to $576 million and grew 4 percent to $2.2 billion for the year.
In its networks and broadcasting operations, Viacom said earnings before taxes and other items jumped 40 percent to $253 million.
MTV Networks pretax earnings rose 45 percent to $176 million, mainly due to higher advertising and affiliate revenues. Ad revenues were boosted by continued ratings growth at Nickelodeon, it said.

The entertainment segment benefited in the fourth quarter from Paramount Pictures' feature films and first run syndication television programming. This led to a 97 percent rise in pretax earnings to $81 million, Viacom said.
Among the company's releases were "Mission: Impossible," and domestic theatrical release of "Star Trek: First Contact," "The First Wives Club" and "Beavis and Butt-Head Do America," the company said.
The quarter also benefited from higher U.S. syndication revenues for television programming, mainly "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine."
Viacom's stock rose 75 cents to $36.75 on the American Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
